tools.name: auto_clock_ins
tools.description:
Auto-generate clock-in records based on schedule (managers only). Resolve the employee by name
using 'employee_name' — never ask the user for an ID. If multiple employees match, the tool
returns the options so you can ask which one and call again with a more specific name.
Returns the generated records.

date.description: The date to generate clock ins for in YYYY-MM-DD format

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use employee_name.

employee_name.description: Employee name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the employee.

tools.name: list_absence_categories
tools.description:
List all available leave categories. Use to resolve a category by name before creating
an absence. Concise lists names and whether they discount leave days; detailed adds
description and a system id.

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives each category name and Discounts leave days. 'detailed' adds the description (when present) and a system id.

tools.name: list_absences
tools.description:
List absences. Default scope is 'mine' (current user's own absences).
Use scope='team' when the user asks about their team ('who is off this week').
Use scope='office' for office-wide data. Use scope='all' for all accessible absences.
Filter by date range using start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD format).
If no dates provided, defaults to the current year.
For "this week", "this month", or "today", call get_current_datetime first, then pass
start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD. Do not invent dates.
Resolve employee/team by name before using their ID as filter.

approved.description: Approval status filter: 0 = pending, 1 = approved, 2 = rejected. Leave blank for all statuses

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID

employee_name.description: Filter by employee name (partial match). Use when asking about a specific employee's data.

name.description: Search by employee name or email

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives the category, date range, total days and approval status. It names the person only when listing someone else's absences (scope is not mine). 'detailed' adds start and end hours, whether it is all-day, the description (when present) and a system id.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all data the user has access to. When the user says 'my expenses' use 'mine'. When they say 'team expenses' or 'who in my team...' use 'team'. When they ask about 'the office' or 'our office' use 'office'. When ambiguous or asking in plural without specifying, use 'all'.

status.description: Status filter for search: 1 = approved, 2 = pending, 3 = rejected

tools.name: list_clock_ins
tools.description:
List clock-in/activity records for an employee. Shows daily summaries with total hours,
contract hours, and extra hours. Filter by date range using start_date and end_date
(YYYY-MM-DD). If no dates provided, defaults to the current week.
When the user says 'my hours' or 'how much have I worked', call this without employee_id.
To see another employee's hours, resolve their name first and pass employee_id.

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID. Only available for managers. If not specified, shows current employee's activities

employee_name.description: Filter by employee name (partial match). Use when asking about a specific employee's data.

end_date.description: End date for filtering (YYYY-MM-DD format). Defaults to end of current week

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). Clock-in records can only be viewed per employee. For team/office/all scope, a summary message will be returned instead.

start_date.description: Start date for filtering (YYYY-MM-DD format). Defaults to start of current week

tools.name: list_competencies
tools.description: List all available competencies for the current employee's account

tools.name: create_competency
tools.description: Create a new competency with its evaluation scale and optionally set target levels per job category

description.description: Detailed description of what this competency measures

grid_box.description: Classification: 'performance' for current results, 'potential' for growth capacity, 'excluded' for inactive

range_to.description: Maximum value of evaluation scale (e.g., 4 for 0-4 scale, 10 for 0-10 scale)

tiers.description: Optional: Target levels per job category. If not provided, no role-specific expectations will be set.

job_category_name.description: Name of the job category (e.g., 'Manager', 'Worker', 'Senior Manager'). Use list_job_categories to see available options.

target_value.description: Expected target level for this role (must be within the competency's range)

values.description: Rating scale values for this competency. Must include one value for each point in the range.

description.description: Detailed description of what this level means

label.description: Label for this value (e.g., 'Poor', 'Below Average', 'Good', 'Very Good', 'Outstanding')

value.description: Numeric value (must match the range, e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 for a 0-4 scale)

tools.name: get_competency
tools.description: Get a competency and its values and tiers by its name

name.description: The name of the competency to get

tools.name: update_competency
tools.description: Update a competency by its ID, you can update the name, description, grid box, range from and range to, if you do not provide a specific value then the current value will be kept

competency_id.description: The ID of the competency to update

description.description: The updated description of the competency

grid_box.description: The updated grid box of the competency

name.description: The updated name of the competency

range_from.description: The updated range from of the competency

range_to.description: The updated range to of the competency

tools.name: toggle_competency
tools.description: Toggle the active status of a competency by its ID

competency_id.description: The ID of the competency to toggle

tools.name: update_competency_value
tools.description: Update a competency value by its ID, you can update the label and/or description

competency_value_id.description: The ID of the competency value to update

description.description: The updated description of the competency value

label.description: The updated label of the competency value

tools.name: update_competency_tier
tools.description: Update a competency tier by its ID, you can update the target value and/or the job category. You can list the job categories with the list_job_categories tool.

competency_id.description: The ID of the competency to which the competency tier belongs

competency_tier_id.description: The ID of the competency tier to update

job_category_id.description: The updated job category of the competency tier

target_value.description: The updated target value of the competency tier

tools.name: list_job_categories
tools.description:
List all available job categories. Use to resolve a job category by name.
Returns category names — use the name for entity resolution, never expose the ID.

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives each category name and whether it is active. 'detailed' adds the description (when present) and a system id. This list is active categories only.

tools.name: list_employees
tools.description:
The staff directory: who works here, and what is on record for them.
Answers about several people at once — a team, an office, or everybody — in a single call.
Use it both to resolve a name the user mentioned and to gather data about a group;
ask for one person with get_employee only when you need that one person.
Only active employees. Archived or deleted ones are not included and cannot be searched.
Filter by name (partial match), team, office, or company. The name filter searches
both name and email.

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID

name.description: Search by employee name, email, team name, or office name (minimum 3 characters)

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives name, email, team and office. 'detailed' adds, for every employee listed, their available leave days, contract, job position and working category — use it to answer about the whole list at once instead of asking for each person separately. Contract and leave detail only appear for employees you manage.

tools.name: list_employee_tasks
tools.description:
List tasks. Default scope is 'mine' (current user's own tasks).
Use scope='team' when the user asks about their team's tasks.
Optionally filter by date range using start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
to show only tasks with deadlines in that range.
If no dates provided, returns all pending tasks regardless of deadline.
For "this week" or any deadline range anchored to now, call get_current_datetime first,
then pass start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD. Do not invent dates.
Defaults to pending tasks. Shows progress percentage and deadlines.

employee_id.description: The ID of the employee whose tasks to retrieve (optional, defaults to current employee)

end_date.description: End date for filtering tasks by deadline (YYYY-MM-DD format)

name.description: Search by task name or tag (minimum 3 characters)

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives the name, status, progress, deadline and tags when present. It names the assignee only when listing someone else's tasks (scope is not mine). 'detailed' adds description, start date, task list, category, tags, assignee and a system id.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all data the user has access to. When the user says 'my tasks' use 'mine'. When they say 'team tasks' use 'team'. When ambiguous or asking in plural without specifying, use 'all'.

start_date.description: Start date for filtering tasks by deadline (YYYY-MM-DD format)

status.description: Filter by task status (optional, defaults to 'pending')

task_list_id.description: Filter by specific task list ID

tools.name: list_expense_categories
tools.description:
List all available expense categories. Use to resolve a category by name before creating
an expense. Returns category names — use the name for entity resolution, never expose the ID.

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives each category name and icon. 'detailed' adds the description (when present) and a system id.

tools.name: list_expenses
tools.description:
List expenses. Default scope is 'mine' (current user's own expenses).
Use scope='team' when the user asks about their team's expenses.
Use scope='office' for office-wide data. Use scope='all' for all accessible expenses.
Filter by date range using start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD format).
If no dates provided, defaults to the current month.
For "this year", "last month", or "this month", call get_current_datetime first, then pass
start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD. Do not invent dates.
Status filter: 0=pending, 1=approved, 2=rejected.

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID

employee_name.description: Filter by employee name (partial match). Use when asking about a specific employee's data.

expense_category_id.description: Filter by specific expense category ID

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives the name, category, date, amount and approval status. It names the filer only when listing someone else's expenses (scope is not mine). 'detailed' adds tax (when present), always names the employee, and a system id.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all data the user has access to. When the user says 'my expenses' use 'mine'. When they say 'team expenses' or 'who in my team...' use 'team'. When they ask about 'the office' or 'our office' use 'office'. When ambiguous or asking in plural without specifying, use 'all'.

status.description: Approval status filter: 0 = pending, 1 = approved, 2 = rejected. Leave blank for all statuses

tools.name: list_items
tools.description: List catalog items. Filter by name, item_category_id, or schedulable. Use detailed format only when an item ID is needed for a follow-up edit.

name.description: Search by name, barcode, or serial number.

response_format.description: concise by default; detailed includes system IDs.

schedulable.description: Filter items that can be scheduled/booked.

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description:
List goals. Default scope is 'mine' (current user's own goals).
Use scope='team' for team goals. Use scope='office' for office-wide.
Use scope='all' for all accessible goals.
Optionally filter by date range using start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD).
If no dates provided, returns all goals regardless of date.
For "this quarter", "past goals", or any range anchored to now, call get_current_datetime
first, then pass start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD. Do not invent dates.
Filter by status (array: planning, active, achieved, missed, discarded),
name (partial match). Use for entity resolution before editing.
Use employee_name to look up goals for a specific employee by name.

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID. Use when you already have the ID from a previous tool call.

employee_name.description: Filter by employee name (partial match). Use when asking about a specific employee's goals. Resolves the employee first, then filters.

end_date.description: Filter goals ending before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives the name, status, progress and end date. It names the owner only when listing someone else's goals (scope is not mine). 'detailed' adds description, target, start date, owner, metrics and a system id.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all data the user has access to. When the user says 'my goals' use 'mine'. When they say 'team goals' use 'team'. When ambiguous or asking in plural without specifying, use 'all'.

start_date.description: Filter goals starting from this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: list_goal_comments
tools.description:
List comments and status updates for a goal. Find the goal by name using 'find_by_name'
(partial match, case-insensitive) — never ask the user for an ID. If multiple goals match,
the tool returns the options so you can ask which one and call again with a more specific name.
Shows progress updates chronologically.

approved.description: Filter by approval status (defaults to approved only)

employee_id.description: Filter by employee ID who created the comment

end_date.description: Filter comments created before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

find_by_name.description: Find the goal by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the goal.

goal_id.description: Goal ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use find_by_name.

metric_id.description: Filter by metric ID associated with the comment

start_date.description: Filter comments created from this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description:
List employee schedules and availability (managers/admins only). Shows working hours
per day for the specified period. Requires start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD).
When the user asks 'team schedules' or 'who is working this week', use scope='team'.
Resolve employee/team by name first.

employee_id.description: Filter by specific employee ID

end_date.description: End date for the availability period in YYYY-MM-DD format

name.description: Search by employee name, email, team name, or office name (minimum 3 characters)

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own data (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all data the user has access to. When the user asks 'team schedules' use 'team'. When they ask about 'the office' use 'office'.

start_date.description: Start date for the availability period in YYYY-MM-DD format

tools.name: list_schedule_catalog
tools.description:
List the assignable work schedules in the company catalog (managers/admins only): the
schedule categories with their weekly hour patterns, plus any rotating shifts (turnos).
Call this BEFORE assigning a schedule so you offer the REAL options — never invent
schedules, shifts or hours. A "turno de mañana/tarde" is usually just a category here.
Optionally filter by name.

name.description: Filter by category or shift name (partial match). Example: 'tarde', 'oficina'.

response_format.description: Use 'concise' (default) for the overview: one line per currently-valid schedule. Use 'detailed' for the full per-day breakdown, validity dates, weekly totals and shift rotations — detailed ALSO lists non-active schedules (expired/upcoming). Combine with 'name' to drill into one schedule.

tools.name: list_reschedules
tools.description:
List reschedule requests (shift-change requests). Mirrors the web: an employee sees their own
requests; a manager sees their reportees' plus their own. Optionally filter by 'employee_name'
(useful for managers) and by 'approved' status. Defaults to the current year.
Internal ids are never shown — to edit one, call update_reschedule with its date.

approved.description: Filter by approval: true = approved, false = not yet approved (pending/rejected). Omit for all statuses.

employee_name.description: Filter by employee name (partial match). Useful for a manager looking at a specific reportee.

start_date.description: Start of date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the start of the current year.

tools.name: create_absence
tools.description:
Create one or more absence requests. Executes immediately — there is NO preview/confirm step.

Target employee (managers only): to create for another person, pass 'employee_name' (preferred)
or 'employee_id'. Omit both to create for the current user. Never ask the user for an ID —
resolve the name here. If the name is ambiguous the tool returns the options so you can ask which
one and call again with a more specific name.

Category: pass 'absence_category_name' (partial match) — never ask for an ID. Resolve it with
list_absence_categories when unsure.

Dates: for a single day or a contiguous run, pass 'start_on'/'end_on'. For SEVERAL separate days
(e.g. "1 hour on the 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th"), pass 'dates' (a list of YYYY-MM-DD) — one
absence is created per day, which keeps a partial-hour absence counted per day. Do NOT collapse
separate days into a single start_on..end_on range: a range charges the days in between in full.

Hours: for a partial-day absence pass 'start_hour' and 'end_hour' (HH:MM); 'all_day' is then
treated as false automatically. Otherwise the absence is all-day.

Attachments: if the user attached a supporting document in the chat (e.g. a medical note),
pass its ref in 'attachment_refs' to file it with the absence. With several days, the
document is filed with every absence created.

absence_category_id.description: The ID of the leave category. Use absence_category_name instead when possible.

absence_category_name.description: Category name (partial match). Alternative to absence_category_id. Use this when the user mentions a category by name.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day absence. Defaults to true. Automatically treated as false when start_hour/end_hour are given.

approved.description: Whether to automatically approve the absence. Defaults to false. Only available for managers and admins.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass them to file those documents with the absence (e.g. a medical note). Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

dates.description: List of individual days (YYYY-MM-DD). Creates one absence per day. Use for non-contiguous days or a per-day time window; do NOT turn separate days into a start_on..end_on range.

description.description: Optional description or reason for the absence

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — prefer employee_name. Omit to create for yourself.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee to create the absence for (managers only). Preferred over employee_id. Omit to create for yourself.

end_hour.description: End time in HH:MM format (for a partial-day absence)

end_on.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional — defaults to start_on for a single-day absence. Ignored when 'dates' is given.

start_hour.description: Start time in HH:MM format (for a partial-day absence)

start_on.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with end_on for a single day or a contiguous range. Ignored when 'dates' is given.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description:
File one or more documents the user attached in the chat (PDF or image) into the employee
document archive (contracts, payslips, certificates…). Executes immediately — there is NO
preview/confirm step.

Requires at least one ref in 'attachment_refs' — the file IS the document. One document is
created per file. Without 'name', each document takes its file's filename.

Category: optional. Pass 'document_category_name' (partial match) — never ask for an ID.
Resolve it with list_document_categories when unsure. Omit it to file without category.

Target employee (managers only): to file in another person's archive, pass 'employee_name'
(preferred) or 'employee_id'. Omit both to file in your own. Never ask the user for an ID —
resolve the name here. If the name is ambiguous the tool returns the options so you can ask
which one and call again with a more specific name.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of the documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Required — one document is filed per ref. Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

document_category_id.description: The ID of the document category. Use document_category_name instead when possible.

document_category_name.description: Category name (partial match). Alternative to document_category_id. Use this when the user mentions a category by name.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — prefer employee_name. Omit to file into your own archive.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee whose archive to file into (managers only). Preferred over employee_id. Omit to file into your own.

name.description: Optional name for the document(s). Defaults to each file's filename.

tools.name: list_document_categories
tools.description:
List all available document categories. Use to resolve a category by name before filing
a document with create_document. Returns category names — use the name for entity
resolution, never expose the ID.

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) gives the category names. 'detailed' adds the description (when present) and a system id.

tools.name: create_expense
tools.description:
Create a new expense. Resolve category by name using list_expense_categories — never ask for an ID.
Returns the created expense details. Defaults: date = today, tax = 0.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass them to file those documents with the expense (e.g. the receipt). Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

expense_category_id.description: The ID of the expense category. Use expense_category_name instead when possible.

expense_category_name.description: Category name (partial match). Alternative to expense_category_id. Use this when the user mentions a category by name.

generated_on.description: The date the expense was generated in YYYY-MM-DD format

tax_amount.description: The tax amount for the expense (optional, defaults to 0)

total.description: The total amount of the expense

tools.name: create_item
tools.description: Create a catalog item (a product/service in the catalogue). Resolve the category by ID or name. This is NOT how you order goods from a provider — for a purchase order ('pedido') use create_purchase_order.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description:
Create a new goal. Only the name is required — all other fields have defaults.
Returns the created goal details. Defaults: status = planning, start_on = today.
Supports metrics as array of {name, value} objects.

description.description: Goal description

tools.name: create_goal_status_update
tools.description:
Post a progress update (status update) on a goal. Use this whenever the user REPORTS PROGRESS —
e.g. "I completed 8 of 10 modules", "I finished the report", "I'm at 80%". Do NOT use edit_goal
for progress updates; edit_goal is only for changing a goal's definition (name, status, dates).
Find the goal by name with 'find_by_name' — never ask the user for an ID. If the goal has a
single metric it is used automatically; if it has several, pass 'metric_name' (otherwise the
tool returns the options so you can ask which one). If the goal has no metrics, omit metric
fields and still pass 'progress' so the goal chart updates. Include 'progress' when reporting
a numeric update. No preview needed — this is a quick action.

description.description: Status update description (required)

find_by_name.description: Find the goal by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the goal.

goal_id.description: Goal ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use find_by_name.

metric_id.description: Metric ID. Optional — prefer metric_name, or omit when the goal has a single metric.

metric_name.description: Metric name (partial match). Only needed when the goal has more than one metric.

progress.description: Progress percentage (0-100). Required when updating a metric.

tools.name: list_goal_actions
tools.description:
List Actions (checklist items) on a goal, grouped by list.
This is not a project task board. For project tasks use `list_employee_tasks`.

goal_id.description: Goal ID from a previous tool response.

response_format.description: concise for a checklist, detailed for IDs and due dates.

tools.name: create_goal_action
tools.description:
Create an Action (checklist item) on a goal. This is not a project task.
Use for breaking a goal into simple todos. For project work use `create_task`.
For a private personal list use `create_personal_todo`.

goal_id.description: Goal ID from a previous tool response.

goal_name.description: Goal name (partial match). Preferred when you do not already have an ID.

list_name.description: Optional Actions list name. Defaults to the first list, or creates a Checklist list.

tools.name: update_goal_action
tools.description:
Update an Action on a goal: rename, due date, complete/uncomplete, or move lists.
This is not a project task. For project tasks use `update_task`.

action_id.description: Action ID from a previous tool response.

due_on.description: New due date (YYYY-MM-DD), or null to clear it.

find_by_name.description: Action name (partial match) on that goal.

goal_id.description: Goal ID from a previous tool response.

list_name.description: Move the action to this list (partial match or new list name).

tools.name: delete_goal_action
tools.description: Delete an Action (checklist item) on a goal. This is not a project task.

action_id.description: Action ID from a previous tool response.

find_by_name.description: Action name (partial match) on that goal.

goal_id.description: Goal ID from a previous tool response.

tools.name: create_clock_in
tools.description:
Create a clock-in record for an employee (managers only). Find the employee by name using
'employee_name' — never ask the user for an ID. If multiple employees match, the tool returns
the options so you can ask which one. Returns the created record details.
Required: employee_name (or employee_id), start_time, end_time, date.

approved.description: Whether to automatically approve the clock in. Defaults to false.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use employee_name.

employee_name.description: Employee name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the employee.

end_on.description: End date of the clock in in YYYY-MM-DD format

start_on.description: Start date of the clock in in YYYY-MM-DD format

task_id.description: Optional ID of the task this clock in is associated with. Use list_employee_tasks to see available options.

tools.name: create_reschedule
tools.description:
Create a request to change an employee's schedule or swap shifts. Resolve employee by name if needed.
Returns the created reschedule details. The request will need manager approval.

employee_name.description: Employee the request is for (partial match). Defaults to yourself; managers can name a team member.

end_on.description: End date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must be greater than or equal to start_on. Required.

other_employee_name.description: Name of the colleague to swap shifts with (partial match).

schedule_category_name.description: Name of the schedule/category to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

shift_name.description: Name of the shift to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

start_on.description: Start date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Cannot be in the past. Required.

tools.name: edit_goal
tools.description:
Edit a goal. Find by name using 'find_by_name' (partial match, case-insensitive) or by goal_id
from a previous tool response. If multiple goals match, present options to the user.
Only changed fields are updated — omitted fields stay unchanged.
Metrics: omit ID to add new, include ID to update, set _destroy to remove.
If you don't have the goal_id and can't identify the goal by name, FIRST call list_goals to find it, THEN call edit_goal.

description.description: Goal description

find_by_name.description: Find by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Alternative to using the ID directly.

goal_id.description: Goal ID to edit. Either goal_id or find_by_name is required.

_destroy.description: Set to true to delete this metric

tools.name: edit_item
tools.description: Edit a catalog item. Find by item_id or find_by_name.

find_by_name.description: Search item by name, barcode, or serial number.

tools.name: get_employee_current_activity
tools.description:
Check if an employee is currently clocked in and what activity they're doing.
Find the employee by name using 'employee_name' — never ask the user for an ID.
If multiple employees match, the tool returns the options so you can ask which one.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use employee_name.

employee_name.description: Employee name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the employee.

tools.name: get_employee_schedule
tools.description:
Get an employee's schedule for a date range. Defaults to current week. For other employees,
requires manager permission. Shows daily working hours and availability.

employee_id.description: The ID of the employee whose schedule to retrieve (optional, defaults to current employee)

end_date.description: End date for date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional, used with start_date)

start_date.description: Start date for date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional, used with end_date)

tools.name: get_task_todos
tools.description:
Get the to-do checklist for a task. Find the task by name using 'find_by_name'
(partial match, case-insensitive) — never ask the user for an ID. If multiple tasks match,
the tool returns the options so you can ask which one and call again with a more specific name.

find_by_name.description: Find the task by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the task.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for summaries and tables. Use 'detailed' when the user asks for specifics about a particular record or when you need IDs for follow-up operations.

task_id.description: Task ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use find_by_name.

tools.name: manage_schedule
tools.description:
Unified tool for schedule changes. Routes to reschedule creation or availability swap
based on context. Returns the result of the schedule operation.

employee_name.description: Employee the change is for (partial match). Defaults to yourself; managers can name a team member.

end_on.description: End date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must be greater than or equal to start_on. Required.

other_employee_name.description: Name of the colleague to swap shifts with (partial match).

schedule_category_name.description: Name of the schedule/category to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

shift_name.description: Name of the shift to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

start_on.description: Start date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Cannot be in the past. Required.

tools.name: start_activity
tools.description:
Start a clock-in / begin working. No preview needed — this is an instant action.
Uses current time by default.

activity_type.description: Use on_call to start the separate on-call activity when an on-call assignment covers the current time.

task_id.description: The ID of a task associated with the employee.

tools.name: stop_activity
tools.description: Stop the current clock-in / end working. No preview needed — instant action. Uses current time.

activity_type.description: Use on_call to stop the separate on-call activity when regular work is also active.

tools.name: swap_availabilities
tools.description:
Swap an employee's schedule between two dates (managers only). Find the employee by name using
'employee_name' — never ask the user for an ID. If multiple employees match, the tool returns
the options so you can ask which one. Returns the swap result details.

destination_date.description: Destination date in YYYY-MM-DD format to which to swap the availability

employee_id.description: ID of the employee whose availabilities to swap. Use list_employees to see available options.

employee_name.description: Employee name (partial match, case-insensitive). Preferred way to identify the employee.

origin_date.description: Origin date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which to swap the availability

tools.name: assign_schedule
tools.description:
Assign a work schedule (a category from the catalog) to an employee or a whole team, for a
date range (managers/admins only). Use list_schedule_catalog FIRST to get the real category
names — never invent a schedule. Resolve the employee/team and the category BY NAME.

Two modes, inferred from the dates:
- TEMPORARY override: pass start_on AND end_on (e.g. "next week") — applies only for that range,
  the previous schedule resumes automatically afterwards.
- PERMANENT change: pass start_on with NO end_on (e.g. "from Monday on") — this REPLACES the
  current schedule from that date and closes the previous one. Make this explicit to the user.

Shows a preview; nothing is applied until confirm_action.

employee_name.description: Employee to assign it to (partial match). Use this OR team_name.

end_on.description: Last day of the schedule (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for a PERMANENT change that replaces the current schedule. Include for a TEMPORARY override.

schedule_category_name.description: Name of the schedule/category to assign (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog. Example: 'Turno de mañana', 'Horario oficina'.

start_on.description: Date the schedule starts (YYYY-MM-DD). Required. Today or future.

team_name.description: Team to assign it to — applies to every active member (partial match). Use this OR employee_name.

tools.name: update_absence
tools.description:
Update an absence request. Find the absence by a day it covers using 'find_by_date'
(any date within the absence period) — never ask the user for an ID. For a manager updating
someone else's absence, also pass 'employee_name'. If several absences match, the tool returns
the options so you can ask which one and call again with a more specific date/employee_name.
Only managers can change approval status. Only changed fields are updated.
To file a supporting document from the chat (e.g. a medical note) with the absence,
pass its ref in 'attachment_refs' — works on its own, without changing any other field.

absence_category_id.description: The ID of the leave category. Use list_absence_categories to see available options. Use holiday/leave as default if none is specified.

absence_id.description: Absence ID. Optional — only if you already have it from a previous tool response. Otherwise use find_by_date.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day absence. Defaults to true.

approved.description: Whether to automatically approve the absence. Defaults to false. Only available for managers and admins.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass them to file those documents with the absence (e.g. a medical note). Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

description.description: Optional description or reason for the absence

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — prefer employee_name.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee whose absence to update (managers only). Combine with find_by_date. Defaults to the current employee.

end_hour.description: End time in HH:MM format (required if all_day is false)

end_on.description: End date of the absence in YYYY-MM-DD format

find_by_date.description: A day the absence covers (YYYY-MM-DD). Preferred way to identify the absence.

start_hour.description: Start time in HH:MM format (required if all_day is false)

start_on.description: Start date of the absence in YYYY-MM-DD format

tools.name: update_clock_in
tools.description:
Update a clock-in record (managers only). Identify the clock-in by 'employee_name' + 'clock_in_date'
(the day it happened) — never ask the user for an ID. If the employee has several clock-ins that day,
also pass 'start_time' (the current start hour you saw in list_clock_ins, e.g. "09:00") to pick one;
otherwise the tool returns the options so you can ask which one.
Then provide the new values: start_on, start_hour, end_on, end_hour (the corrected times).

approved.description: Whether to automatically approve the clock in. Defaults to false.

clock_in_date.description: The day the clock-in to update happened (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with employee_name to find the record.

clock_in_id.description: Clock-in ID. Optional — only if you already have it. Otherwise use employee_name + clock_in_date.

employee_id.description: The ID of the employee whose clock in to update. If not provided, updates the current clock in's employee. Only available for managers.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee whose clock-in to update (partial match). Preferred way to identify the clock-in, with clock_in_date.

end_on.description: End date of the clock in in YYYY-MM-DD format

start_on.description: Start date of the clock in in YYYY-MM-DD format

start_time.description: Current start hour of the target clock-in (HH:MM), as shown in list_clock_ins. Only needed to disambiguate when the employee has several clock-ins that day.

task_id.description: Optional ID of the task this clock in is associated with. Use list_employee_tasks to see available options.

tools.name: update_reschedule
tools.description:
Update a pending reschedule request (shift-change request). Identify it by 'date' (a day the
request covers) — never ask the user for an ID. For a manager editing someone else's request,
also pass 'employee_name'. If several pending requests match, the tool returns the options so
you can ask which one. Use list_reschedules first if you need to see what's pending. Only
pending requests can be updated. Then provide the new values (start_on, end_on, etc.).

date.description: A day the reschedule request covers (YYYY-MM-DD). Preferred way to identify the request.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee whose request to update (managers only). Defaults to the current employee.

end_on.description: New end date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must be greater than or equal to start_on. If not provided, keeps the current end date.

other_employee_name.description: Name of the colleague to swap shifts with (partial match).

schedule_category_name.description: Name of the schedule/category to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

shift_name.description: Name of the shift to change to (partial match), as shown by list_schedule_catalog.

start_on.description: New start date of the reschedule period in YYYY-MM-DD format. Cannot be in the past. If not provided, keeps the current start date.

tools.name: confirm_action
tools.description:
Confirm and execute the action that was previewed just before, as soon as the user approves
it (yes / sí / ok / adelante / hazlo). The end of every preview tells you exactly how to call
this — with no arguments, or with the preview_id it shows. Follow that instruction. Only when
the system reports that there are several pending actions, call it again with `choice` set to
the number of the one to confirm.

choice.description: Only when the system reported several pending actions: the number (1, 2, ...) of the one to confirm.

preview_id.description: The id of the previewed action, when the preview showed one. Pass it exactly as shown.

tools.name: create_changelog
tools.description: Create a new changelog entry for TalentoHQ. Only available for TalentoHQ management.

content.description: The content of the changelog entry (required)

title.description: The title of the changelog entry (required)

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description:
List skills in the company catalog. Search by name or category.
Use expiring_before to find skills with certifications expiring soon.
Examples: 'what skills exist' -> no filters. 'programming skills' -> category_name=Programming.
'expiring certifications' -> expiring_before=2026-06-30.
Shows employee count per skill and expiration rules.

category_name.description: Filter by skill category name (partial match). Examples: 'programming', 'certifications'. Use this when the user asks about a type of skill.

expiring_before.description: Only return skills that have employee certifications expiring before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use when the user asks about expiring or soon-to-expire certifications.

name.description: Search by skill name (partial match). Examples: 'python', 'aws'.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for summaries and tables. Use 'detailed' when the user asks for specifics about a particular skill or when you need IDs for follow-up operations.

tools.name: list_employee_skills
tools.description:
List employee skill assignments. Works in three modes:
1. By employee: 'what skills does Maria have' -> employee_name=Maria
2. By skill: 'who knows Python' -> skill_name=Python, scope=team
3. By scope: 'what skills does my team have' -> scope=team (no employee_name or skill_name)
Default scope is 'mine'. Use scope='team' when asking about team skills.
Shows expiration status (EXPIRED, days remaining) and skill targets.
When the user asks 'my skills' or 'what skills do I have', use scope=mine without employee_name.
When asking about another person, resolve by name with employee_name.
When asking about team/office/all skills without a specific person or skill, use scope only.

employee_id.description: Direct employee ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

employee_name.description: Search skills FOR a specific employee (partial name match). Use when the user says 'what skills does [name] have'. Leave empty for scope-based queries.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for summaries and tables. Use 'detailed' when the user asks for specifics or when you need IDs for follow-up operations.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = current user's own skills (default). 'team' = current user's team. 'office' = current user's office. 'all' = all accessible data. When the user says 'my skills' use 'mine'. When they say 'team skills' or 'who in my team' use 'team'.

skill_id.description: Direct skill ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

skill_name.description: Search employees WITH a specific skill (partial name match). Use when the user says 'who knows [skill]' or 'who has [skill]'.

tools.name: list_appointments
tools.description:
List appointments booked through the company's booking calendars (the public
scheduling pages where clients, candidates or other guests pick a slot to meet
an employee). An appointment is a scheduled meeting with a named guest. Use
this tool for any question about these scheduled meetings, however the user
happens to phrase it.

Results span every calendar the user can access; you never need to name a
calendar first. Use calendar_name only to narrow to one specific calendar.

Scope of what to return:
- kind selects which calendars count: general (normal booking calendars),
  interviews (recruiting/selection calendars), or all. Choose it from what the
  user is asking about, not from a fixed rule.
- status filters by lifecycle state. With no status you get the actionable
  agenda: confirmed appointments inside the date window, plus every pending one
  (the approval queue) whatever its date, so nothing awaiting the user is missed.
- The date window defaults to from today for ~30 days and bounds the confirmed
  results. To look further back or ahead (e.g. past cancellations), set
  start_date/end_date explicitly.

Times are shown in each calendar's own timezone and always labelled; report
them to the user as given. Use response_format detailed when the user wants
specifics or you may need to act on a specific appointment next.

calendar_name.description: Restrict to a single calendar by name (partial match). Omit to span all accessible calendars.

end_date.description: End of the date window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to ~30 days after the start.

invitee_name.description: Filter to appointments whose guest (invitee) name matches (partial, accent-insensitive). Use when the user asks about a specific person's appointment(s) and no single calendar is named.

kind.description: Which calendars to include. 'general' = normal booking calendars (default). 'interviews' = recruiting/selection calendars (choose when the subject is hiring/candidates). 'all' = both (choose when the request isn't limited to one kind).

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) for summaries; 'detailed' for full data and when you might act on a specific appointment next.

start_date.description: Start of the date window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today. Set an earlier date to include past appointments.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle state. Omit to get the actionable agenda (confirmed + pending). Use 'pending' for what awaits approval, 'cancelled'/'declined' for the corresponding history.

tools.name: get_appointment
tools.description:
Show the full detail of a single appointment (a meeting booked through a
booking calendar): guest, contact, hosts, timing, status, source and any note
attached to it (for example a message left when it was created, approved,
declined or cancelled).

Identify the appointment the way a person would: by the calendar it belongs to
plus the guest's name, optionally narrowed by date. If a previous listing
already surfaced an internal appointment id, you may pass it directly instead —
prefer the human identifiers, fall back to the id only when name+date is
ambiguous or awkward. If more than one appointment matches, the tool asks you
to narrow it down.

Times are shown in the calendar's timezone and always labelled.

appointment_id.description: Internal appointment id from a previous detailed listing. Optional shortcut; the human identifiers above are preferred.

calendar_name.description: Name of the calendar the appointment belongs to (partial match). Use together with invitee_name.

date.description: Optional appointment date (YYYY-MM-DD) to disambiguate when a guest has several bookings.

invitee_name.description: Name of the guest who booked (partial match). Use together with calendar_name.

tools.name: manage_appointment
tools.description:
Decide on an existing appointment: approve, decline or cancel it. Every decision
emails the guest, so this returns a preview first and applies nothing until you
confirm it. Only call it once the user has clearly asked to act on a specific
appointment. If they are still choosing which one, or only asking about it,
don't act yet: identify the appointment and the intended action first.

Which actions are possible depends on the appointment's current state, so read
it (or list appointments) when unsure:
- approve turns a pending (or previously cancelled) appointment into confirmed.
- decline rejects an appointment that is still pending.
- cancel calls off a confirmed or pending appointment, freeing the slot.
If the requested action doesn't fit the current state, the tool explains why
instead of acting.

Identify the appointment by calendar name + guest name (optionally a date), or
by an internal id from a previous detailed listing. When approving or declining,
an optional message can be sent to the guest along with the decision;
cancellations send a standard notice and cannot carry a message.

action.description: The decision to apply. 'approve' confirms a pending/cancelled appointment; 'decline' rejects a pending one; 'cancel' calls off a confirmed/pending one.

appointment_id.description: Internal appointment id from a previous detailed listing. Optional shortcut; human identifiers preferred.

calendar_name.description: Name of the calendar the appointment belongs to (partial match). Use with invitee_name.

client_message.description: Optional message shared with the guest when approving or declining. Ignored on cancel — the guest receives a standard cancellation notice.

invitee_name.description: Name of the guest who booked (partial match). Use with calendar_name.

tools.name: create_appointment
tools.description:
Book an appointment manually on one of the company's general booking calendars —
for example when arranging a meeting on someone's behalf. It creates a confirmed
appointment straight away and (optionally) emails the guest; there is no separate
confirmation step, so only call it once the user has clearly asked to book, with
the guest, date and time settled. While details are still being discussed, hold
off and gather them first.

This is for general calendars only. Interview/recruiting calendars are booked by
the candidate through their invitation, not created here.

Times are interpreted in the calendar's own timezone. Hosts default to how the
calendar is configured (its single host, or all required hosts) — only pass
host names to override that. If the requested slot clashes with a host's
existing booking, the tool reports it instead of double-booking. If you are not
sure a time is actually free, check the calendar's open times first
(list_appointment_slots) rather than guessing one.

calendar_name.description: Name of the general booking calendar to book on (partial match).

client_message.description: Optional note stored with the appointment.

end_time.description: End time (HH:MM), in the calendar's timezone.

host_names.description: Optional. Names of the hosts to assign. Omit to use the calendar's default hosts. Every name must be an active host of the calendar.

invitee_email.description: Optional guest email (needed if you want them to receive the confirmation).

invitee_name.description: Name of the guest the appointment is for.

send_confirmation.description: Whether to email the guest a confirmation. Default false; set true only when the user explicitly wants the guest emailed.

start_time.description: Start time (HH:MM), in the calendar's timezone.

tools.name: list_appointment_slots
tools.description:
Show the free time slots a booking calendar currently offers, so you can propose
real, bookable times before creating an appointment. Availability is derived from
the hosts' working schedules minus their existing bookings, and respects the
calendar's rules (duration, notice, buffers, horizon) — so only genuinely
open slots are returned.

Name the calendar you want (this is most useful for the general calendars you can
book on). The window defaults to about a week from today; widen it with
start_date/end_date when the user needs times further out. Slots are shown grouped
by day, in the calendar's timezone.

calendar_name.description: Name of the booking calendar to check (partial match).

end_date.description: Last day to check (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to about a week after the start.

start_date.description: First day to check (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.

tools.name: create_survey
tools.description:
Create a survey (poll, feedback, climate or NPS) with its questions in one step. Audience, frequency,
notification, and activation are optional arguments on this call — do not send the user to the admin
panel for them. The same arguments are on update_survey for a survey that already exists.

It is created as a DRAFT unless activate is true. A draft collects nothing. With no audience, only the
owner is a respondent. notify_respondents defaults to false, so activation does not email anyone until
that flag is true. Activation is the admin Activate button: the survey becomes active, or scheduled
when the next round is still in the future.

If the user is still deciding the questions, write the questionnaire with them first. Create as soon
as the questions are specified, and pass audience, frequency, notification, and activate only when
the user has already decided those. Do not invent an activation.

For NPS surveys: pass name and nps_question — the 0-10 scale is created automatically. Do not pass sections.
For poll/feedback/climate: pass sections with questions. Each question needs a text and type.

Question types:
- 'rating': a numeric scale (e.g., 1-5 stars). Set 'scale' (3-10, default 5). Options are created automatically.
- 'selection': multiple choice. Pass 'options' as an array of strings.
- 'yes_no': binary choice. Automatically creates Yes/No options.
- 'text': open text response. No options needed.
- 'date_time': date and/or time response. Set 'datetime_response_type' to only_date, only_time, or date_and_time.

Examples:
- "create a survey about workplace safety" → type=feedback, suggest 5-8 questions mixing rating and text
- "create an NPS survey for the onboarding program" → type=nps, nps_question="How likely are you to recommend our onboarding program to a new colleague?"
- "make a poll about the office party" → type=poll, short with 2-3 selection questions

tools.name: create_onboarding_template

Create an onboarding process template with actions/tasks.
Use when the user wants to design an onboarding plan, create onboarding steps, or set up a new hire checklist.

Template are automatically assigned to new employees based on visibility rules.
The user cannot start an onboarding for a specific employee through this tool.

Actions define what needs to happen and when, relative to the employee's start date:
- phase 'before_start': action happens X days/weeks/months BEFORE the employee starts
- phase 'after_start': action happens X days/weeks/months AFTER the employee starts
- days=0 with after_start: action happens on the start date itself

Examples:
- "create an onboarding for developers" → name="Developer Onboarding", actions with setup laptop, IDE, repo access, etc.
- "create a simple onboarding checklist" → name="General Onboarding", 5-7 common actions
- "make an onboarding with tasks before and after start" → mix of before_start and after_start phases

Suggest a good set of actions when the user gives a vague request. Think about:
- Before start: equipment setup, accounts creation, workspace preparation
- First day: welcome, tour, team introduction, paperwork
- First week: training, tools setup, buddy introduction
- First month: 30-day check-in, goal setting, feedback session

actions.description: List of onboarding actions/tasks. Each action defines WHAT needs to happen, WHEN (relative to start date), and WHO is responsible.

days.description: Number of days/weeks/months before or after start date. Default: 0.

description.description: Detailed description of what needs to be done.

name.description: Action name. Short and clear. Must be unique within the template.

needs_approval.description: Whether action needs manager approval. Default: false.

phase.description: When relative to start date. 'before_start' = before arrival. 'after_start' = after start (default).

responsible.description: Who performs this action. 'direct' = the new employee themselves (default). 'team_manager' = their team manager. 'office_manager' = the office manager. 'specific' = a named employee (requires responsible_employee_name with a real person's name, NOT a department like 'HR').

responsible_employee_name.description: ONLY when responsible='specific'. Name of the person responsible (partial match).

send_notification.description: Send email notification when action is due. Default: false.

name.description: Template name. Descriptive and specific. Example: 'Engineering Team Onboarding', 'Sales New Hire Checklist'

To add actions: pass them in 'add_actions' (same format as create).
To remove actions: pass action names in 'remove_actions'.
To rename: pass new 'name'.

You can add and remove actions in the same call.
Action names must be unique within the template — adding a duplicate name will fail.

Examples:
- "add a 90-day review to the engineering onboarding" → template_name="Engineering", add_actions=[{name: "90-day review", days: 90, phase: "after_start"}]
- "remove the laptop setup from the sales onboarding" → template_name="Sales", remove_actions=["Set up laptop"]
