option_labels.description: Exact option labels for single_select or multi_select fields.

value.description: Value for boolean, date, time, datetime, string, text, number, or currency fields. Use an empty string or null to clear optional scalar fields.

find_by_name.description: Search the provider by name, legal name, tax ID or email.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description:
List sales invoices the user can access — exactly the set they see in the web (same visibility). Filter by status, invoice type, customer name, issue-date range or catalog item.
Status defaults to "draft" when not specified. Use status "sent" for issued invoices, "cancelled" for annulled ones.
Amounts and totals come straight from the tool — never recompute them. Use detailed format only when an invoice ID is needed for a follow-up action.

id.description: Specific invoice ID for a single lookup.

item_id.description: Only invoices containing this catalog item.

response_format.description: concise by default; detailed includes system IDs and full breakdown.

type_invoice.description: For sent invoices, filter by normal F1, simplified F2, rectificative (R1/R5), or all. Mirrors the web filter.

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description:
Get the full detail of ONE sales invoice: customer, line items, taxes, discounts, retention, totals, payment status and issue/due dates.
Find it by invoice_id, by invoice_number (e.g. "2024-0007"), or by customer name. If a customer has several invoices, this returns the list so you can pick one — use list_invoices to browse a customer's invoices.
All amounts come from the tool; never recompute them.

customer_name.description: Customer name to resolve the invoice from.

tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description:
Create a DRAFT sales invoice after showing a preview with the exact totals. The invoice is NOT issued or sent — it stays as a draft the user finalises in the web.
Supports the same draft fiscal variants as the web form: normal (F1), simplified (F2), rectifications, standard VAT (S1), exempt/no-VAT operations, reverse charge and not-subject operations when available for the account. For VAT, pass a tax_id or percentage; omit it on standard manual lines to use the account's standard VAT rate. VAT-free operations do not require line taxes.
Always present the previewed totals exactly as returned — never calculate amounts or taxes yourself. Requires at least one line.

customer_id.description: Customer ID. Required for F1; optional for F2 and linked without fiscal snapshot details.

customer_name.description: Customer name to resolve. Required for F1; optional for F2.

discount_type.description: Whether the invoice-wide discount is a fixed amount or a percentage.

discount_value.description: Optional invoice-wide discount (applies to the whole invoice).

invoice_format.description: F1 normal invoice or F2 simplified invoice. Defaults to F1.

invoice_kind.description: normal by default; rectification creates R1/R5 from rectified_invoice_id.

invoice_lines.description: Invoice lines. At least one required.

tax_id.description: VAT tax ID. Used before tax_percentage when present.

tax_percentage.description: VAT rate as a number, e.g. 21, 10 or 4. For VAT-free invoices, omit tax fields.

unit_price.description: Unit price. Taken from the catalog item when omitted.

legal_note_id.description: Optional account legal note ID. Omit for default behavior.

rectified_invoice_id.description: Accessible sent invoice ID to rectify when invoice_kind is rectification.

retention_id.description: Optional account retention ID. Omit for default behavior.

type_operation.description: Fiscal operation. Non-Verifactu accounts allow S1/E1; Verifactu accounts allow all listed UI codes.

tools.name: edit_invoice
tools.description:
Edit a DRAFT sales invoice after showing a preview with the recomputed totals. Only draft invoices can be edited — sent, rectified or cancelled invoices are immutable (the user must rectify them in the web).
Find the invoice by invoice_id, by invoice_number, or by find_by_customer. Supports the same draft fiscal fields as the web form: normal/simplified format, rectification kind, fiscal operation, optional retention/legal note, and VAT-free lines.
Present the previewed totals exactly as returned — never calculate amounts yourself.

customer_id.description: Reassign the invoice to this customer ID.

customer_name.description: Reassign the invoice to the customer resolved from this name.

find_by_customer.description: Locate the draft invoice by its customer name (drafts have no number). Used only to find the invoice, not to change it.

invoice_format.description: F1 normal invoice or F2 simplified invoice.

invoice_lines.description: Lines to add/update/remove. Include id to update, omit id to add, set _destroy true to remove.

_destroy.description: Set true (with id) to remove this line.

id.description: Existing line ID (to update or remove).

tax_id.description: VAT tax ID. Used before tax_percentage when present.

tax_percentage.description: VAT rate as a number, e.g. 21, 10 or 4. For VAT-free invoices, omit tax fields.

invoice_number.description: Draft invoice number to resolve (rarely set; drafts usually have none).

legal_note_id.description: Optional account legal note ID. Omit to keep/default; null or blank clears.

rectified_invoice_id.description: Accessible sent invoice ID to rectify when invoice_kind is rectification.

retention_id.description: Optional account retention ID. Omit to keep/default; null or blank clears.

type_operation.description: Fiscal operation. Non-Verifactu accounts allow S1/E1; Verifactu accounts allow all listed UI codes.

tools.name: send_invoice
tools.description:
Issue/send a DRAFT sales invoice after showing a confirmation preview. This finalizes the invoice: it can assign the fiscal invoice number, mark the invoice as sent, confirm stock movements, and for Verifactu accounts request AEAT verification asynchronously.
Find the invoice by invoice_id, by invoice_number, or by find_by_customer. Only draft invoices can be issued. Do not use this tool to edit invoice contents; call edit_invoice first when changes are needed.

find_by_customer.description: Locate the draft invoice by customer name when the user did not provide an ID.

invoice_number.description: Draft invoice number to resolve when present.

tools.name: reopen_invoice
tools.description:
Move a sent sales invoice back to draft after showing a confirmation preview. Use this when the user wants to edit a sent invoice that has not been accepted by Verifactu/AEAT yet.
Find the invoice by invoice_id, by invoice_number, or by find_by_customer. AEAT-accepted, rectified, cancelled, and already-draft invoices cannot be reopened. Invoices with recorded payments or a paid marker also cannot be reopened.
Reopening keeps the assigned invoice number; sending it again will reuse that number instead of generating a new one.

find_by_customer.description: Locate a sent invoice by customer name when the user did not provide an ID or number.

tools.name: list_purchase_orders
tools.description:
List purchase orders ("pedidos") the user can access — exactly the set they see in the web. Filter by status, provider or order date range.
Purchase orders track quantities ordered from providers and carry NO monetary amounts. Use detailed format only when an order ID is needed for a follow-up action.

id.description: Specific purchase order ID for a single lookup.

response_format.description: concise by default; detailed includes system IDs and the full line list.

tools.name: get_purchase_order
tools.description:
Get the full detail of ONE purchase order ("pedido"): provider, status, order date, description, notes and the ordered lines (item and quantity, plus received quantity when applicable).
Find it by purchase_order_id or by order_number. Purchase orders carry no monetary amounts.

tools.name: create_purchase_order
tools.description:
Create a purchase order ("pedido" / orden de compra) after showing a preview. USE THIS whenever the user wants to ORDER, request or buy quantities of goods from a provider — e.g. "crea un pedido a Proveedor X de 5 teclados y 5 ratones". The line item names are free text describing what to order; do NOT create catalog items (create_item) for them.
A purchase order requests quantities from a provider and carries NO monetary amounts. It is created as a draft. Resolve the provider by name or ID (optional). Each line needs an item name and a quantity. Requires at least one line.

purchase_lines.description: Order lines. At least one required.

quantity.description: Quantity ordered. Must be greater than 0.

tools.name: edit_purchase_order
tools.description:
Edit a purchase order ("pedido") after showing a preview. Only editable orders can be changed (draft, rejected, or approved); ordered/received/closed/cancelled orders are locked.
Find it by purchase_order_id or order_number. Provide only the fields to change. For lines: include a line's id to update it, omit the id to add a new line, or set _destroy true (with the id) to remove it.
Editing an already-approved order returns it to draft for re-approval.

provider_name.description: Reassign to the provider resolved from this name.

purchase_lines.description: Lines to add/update/remove. Include id to update, omit id to add, set _destroy true to remove.

_destroy.description: Set true (with id) to remove this line.

id.description: Existing line ID (to update or remove).

tools.name: transition_purchase_order
tools.description:
Move a purchase order ("pedido") to a new status after showing a preview. Use this to submit a draft for approval, mark an order as ordered/received/closed/cancelled, or reopen a rejected order.
Find it by purchase_order_id or order_number. Approving or rejecting an order is NOT done here — that happens through the approval flow in the web. Only transitions valid from the current status are allowed.

new_status.description: Target status: pending_approval (submit for approval), ordered, partially_received, received, closed, cancelled, or draft (reopen a rejected order).

tools.name: list_purchase_invoices
tools.description:
List purchase invoices ("facturas de compra" / facturas de proveedor) the user can access — exactly the set they see in the web. Filter by provider or issue-date range.
A purchase invoice is a bill received FROM a provider: it has a single total and an optional attached document (no line items). Use detailed format only when an invoice ID is needed for a follow-up action.

id.description: Specific purchase invoice ID for a single lookup.

response_format.description: concise by default; detailed includes system IDs.

tools.name: get_purchase_invoice
tools.description:
Get the full detail of ONE purchase invoice ("factura de compra"): provider, issue/due dates, total, payment status, whether a document is attached, and notes.
Find it by purchase_invoice_id or by provider name. If a provider has several purchase invoices, this returns the list so you can pick one.

provider_name.description: Provider name to resolve the invoice from.

tools.name: create_purchase_invoice
tools.description:
Register a purchase invoice ("factura de compra" / factura recibida de un proveedor) after showing a preview. This records a bill RECEIVED from a provider: a single total amount, with no line items.
Resolve the provider by name or ID (required) and give the total (required).
If the user attached the invoice document in the chat (PDF or photo), pass its ref in 'attachment_refs' to file it with the invoice. A purchase invoice holds ONE document — pass only the invoice file's ref.

attachment_refs.description: Ref of the invoice document the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass ONE ref only — the invoice holds a single document. Copy the ref exactly as it appears.

tools.name: edit_purchase_invoice
tools.description:
Edit a purchase invoice ("factura de compra") after showing a preview: change its total, dates or notes, or mark it as paid (set paid_on). Find it by purchase_invoice_id or by provider name.
To set or replace the invoice's document, pass the ref of a file the user attached in the chat in 'attachment_refs' (ONE ref — the invoice holds a single document; a new one replaces the old). Works on its own, without changing any other field. To change the provider, use the web.

attachment_refs.description: Ref of the invoice document the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass ONE ref only — it replaces the invoice's current document. Copy the ref exactly as it appears.

paid_on.description: Mark as paid on this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

provider_name.description: Provider name to resolve the invoice from.

tools.name: list_opportunities
tools.description:
List sales opportunities / deals ("oportunidades") the user can access — exactly the set they see in the web. Filter by status (open/won/lost), customer or pipeline stage.
Each opportunity has an expected amount; use the amounts from the tool, never recompute them. Use detailed format only when an opportunity ID is needed for a follow-up action.

id.description: Specific opportunity ID for a single lookup.

response_format.description: concise by default; detailed includes system IDs.

tools.name: get_opportunity
tools.description:
Get the full detail of ONE sales opportunity / deal: customer, owner, pipeline stage, status, expected amount, probability, expected close date, and (if closed) the closing factor and actual amount.
Find it by opportunity_id or by name. If several match the name, this returns the list so you can pick one.

tools.name: create_opportunity
tools.description:
Create a sales opportunity / deal ("oportunidad"). An opportunity belongs to a customer and sits in a pipeline stage. It opens with status "open".
Resolve the customer by name or ID (required). The stage defaults to the first pipeline stage unless you name one. Give the expected amount and, optionally, the amount period (one-time/monthly/annual), expected close date and probability.

amount_period.description: Recurrence of the amount. Defaults to one_time.

custom_fields.description: CRM custom field values. Use field_uuid, field_id, or exact field_name. Scalar fields use value; datetime values use ISO 8601; select fields use option_ids or option_labels; currency uses value plus optional currency_code.

currency_code.description: Currency code for currency fields, e.g. EUR.

option_ids.description: Option IDs for single_select or multi_select fields. Use an empty array to clear optional selector fields.

option_labels.description: Exact option labels for single_select or multi_select fields.

value.description: Value for boolean, date, time, datetime, string, text, number, or currency fields. Use an empty string or null to clear optional scalar fields.

stage_name.description: Pipeline stage name (defaults to the first stage).

tools.name: edit_opportunity
tools.description:
Edit a sales opportunity / deal: change its name, description, customer, expected amount, amount period, expected close date or probability. Find it by opportunity_id or name.
To MOVE it to a different pipeline stage use change_opportunity_stage; to mark it won/lost use close_opportunity; to reopen use reopen_opportunity. Those are not done here.

custom_fields.description: CRM custom field values. Use field_uuid, field_id, or exact field_name. Scalar fields use value; datetime values use ISO 8601; select fields use option_ids or option_labels; currency uses value plus optional currency_code.

currency_code.description: Currency code for currency fields, e.g. EUR.

option_ids.description: Option IDs for single_select or multi_select fields. Use an empty array to clear optional selector fields.

option_labels.description: Exact option labels for single_select or multi_select fields.

value.description: Value for boolean, date, time, datetime, string, text, number, or currency fields. Use an empty string or null to clear optional scalar fields.

customer_name.description: Reassign to the customer resolved from this name.

tools.name: change_opportunity_stage
tools.description:
Move a sales opportunity / deal to a different pipeline stage. The change is recorded in the opportunity's stage history. Find the opportunity by opportunity_id or name and give the target stage by name.
This does not win/lose the deal — for that use close_opportunity.

note.description: Optional note for the stage change.

tools.name: close_opportunity
tools.description:
Close a sales opportunity / deal as WON or LOST. Find it by opportunity_id or name.
A closing factor (reason) is required. For a WON deal the actual amount and its period are also required. The closed date defaults to today. To undo a close, use reopen_opportunity.

actual_amount.description: Final amount (required when outcome is won).

actual_amount_period.description: Period of the actual amount (required when won).

closed_on.description: Close date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today. Cannot be in the future.

tools.name: reopen_opportunity
tools.description: Reopen a closed (won or lost) sales opportunity / deal, returning it to "open". A note explaining why is required. Find it by opportunity_id or name.

tools.name: list_views
tools.description:
List the public pages that can be customized and, for the current account,
whether each one already has an active custom design. Call this first to
discover the view keys, then call list_versions for one of them.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description:
List the versions of a custom view with their name, status (active, published,
draft, unpublished changes) and last-updated time. Read, preview, write and
edit tools take a version by its NAME (matched ignoring case and accents), so
copy the names from here. Pass a view_key from list_views.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

tools.name: read_view
tools.description:
Read a custom-view version: its master document (verbatim), the tokens
available for that view, and the hard rules for editing it. The returned
master is the ONLY valid base for the "old" snippets you pass to edit_view —
copy from it, never from memory. Read again after any failed edit or at the
start of a new request: the document may have changed in the web editor.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to read (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

tools.name: preview_view
tools.description:
Render a version's current master to HTML against sample data, to check the
resulting design without publishing. variant "normal" fills every token;
variant "sparse" leaves optional tokens empty to confirm the design still
holds when data is missing. Returns the rendered body (the CSS is omitted —
it is already in the master you read) plus a preview_url the user can open in
a browser to see the real render with the account's data and full styling.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

variant.description: Sample data set: "normal" (all tokens) or "sparse" (optional tokens empty). Default: normal.

version.description: Name of the version to preview (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

tools.name: edit_view
tools.description:
Apply changes to a custom-view version's master as an ordered list of literal
{old, new} text replacements. This is where edits to the page are made: each
"old" must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the current master (add surrounding context
to disambiguate) and be copied VERBATIM from the latest read_view or the
master returned by the previous edit — never typed from memory. Use the
shortest unique snippet, not whole blocks: a long "old" fails if a single
character differs.

Use this for targeted changes to the existing design. To rebuild the page
from scratch (a full redesign, or rewriting most of the document), use
write_view instead — recoding the whole document as {old, new} anchors here
would be slow and brittle.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

The edit is atomic and validated server-side: if ANY replacement fails, NONE
are applied and the master is unchanged. On success the full updated master
is returned — base your next edit on it.

On failure the response is an error whose text starts with one of two leads:
- "fixable, try again" (old not found or ambiguous, unknown token, invalid
  CSS): adjust and retry. When an "old" is not found, the error includes the
  closest real region of the document — copy it verbatim. Never resend the
  same batch unchanged.
- "policy limit, do not retry" (scripts, external URLs, iframes, url() in
  CSS): explain the limitation to the user and offer an alternative.

Warnings (non-blocking): missing_apply_button, missing_h1, multiple_h1,
heading_level_skip.

replacements.description: Ordered list of {old, new}; each old must appear exactly once in the master.

old.description: Exact text to replace (must appear exactly once, copied verbatim).

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to edit (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

tools.name: write_view
tools.description: Replace a custom-view version's ENTIRE master with a new document. Use this for a full redesign or when you are rewriting most of the page — NOT for small or targeted changes (for those use edit_view, which is faster and safer for surgical tweaks). Pass the complete new master: HTML + one

master.description: The complete new master document (HTML + one <style> block + token carriers).

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to rewrite (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

tools.name: create_version
tools.description:
Create a new version of a custom view to work on without touching the active
one. By default it starts from the page's default template (the same starting
point the web editor calls "Basic template"); pass "from" (the name of an
existing version) to start from a copy of that version instead.

The new version is a private draft: it is not active and not published, so it
never affects the public page. Publishing and activating stay in the web
editor. After creating, use read_view / write_view / edit_view / preview_view
with the new version's name.

from.description: Optional: name of an existing version to copy the design from. Omit to start from the seed.

name.description: Name for the new version (must be unique for this view), e.g. "Rediseño verano".

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.
